title: setPool repoints _pairToken without re-validating stored custom _primeToPairPath (stale path can route swap to wrong token)
description: setPool repoints _pairToken without clearing or re-asserting the stored custom _primeToPairPath. A stored path whose end token no longer matches the repointed _pairToken silently violates the setter's own advertised invariant (path end == pairToken).
impact: No theft, no silent value leak. A stale path would route the next pool() swap toward the wrong token -- but this is loud: the next pool() reverts or under-funds against its on-chain minPairOut/minTargetOut floors, and any stranded dust is sweepable via rescueERC20.
attackPath: 1. Owner sets a custom _primeToPairPath ending at the current pair token.
2. Owner later calls setPool to repoint _pairToken without clearing/re-asserting the stored path.
3. The setter silently violates its own advertised invariant (path end == pairToken).
4. Next pool() routes against the stale path -> reverts/under-funds (loud), no silent loss.
recommendation: Clear or re-assert _primeToPairPath inside _setPool when the pair token changes.

classification.likelihood: low; owner-driven, near the obvious line.
classification.recoverable: Yes; re-set the path, sweep dust via rescueERC20.

borderlineNote: Considered Low -- rejected: impact is a revert/under-fund against on-chain floors plus sweepable dust, which is state-handling QA, not a value-leak Low. Not suppressed under KI#1/KI#4: a non-malicious owner could be surprised the stored path is not re-validated (non-obvious enough to surface), but impact ceiling is revert/dust, so QA-bundle note.
